Messages.Author: Whisker
Messages.Body:
Name: Getaway Car
Cardtype: action modifier
Cost: none
Capacity: none
Discipline: none
Clan: none
Requires a minion with a vehicle.
Minions without vehicles or celerity  cannot block this action.

Flavor text: Sure, it only goes like 50 mph. Can you run that fast?

Art notes: Bunch of angry people with weapons trying to catch an icecream truck speeding away.

World of Darkness reference: uh, none.

How does this card address a compelling game need?: Just giving an extra reason to play with vehicles.

Created by: Mikko Moisander

Messages.Author: ReverendRevolver
Messages.Body:
Yea, "cannot block" is rough, you can give Beatrice Trembley and the sun pharoah hawgs and have them hack/strike with conviction for large unblockable bleeds.

To be unblockable, Id say it needs to tap a minion with a vehicle and be a non bleed. Also, wouldnt a getaway only help once youve done something? Like, you get caught trying to burn a powerbase, having an exit strategy doesnt help much, and leads to the premise where this card is either like Zephyr or As the Crow.(which woupd work, but maybe cost a pool or make the vehicle burn or something where the minion takes damage or is only untapped to block, etc)

Cool art notes though...

As well as the power problems other people note (which is not a trivial problem), thematically it seems wrong. A getaway car is about getting away afterwards, whether you succeeded in your bank heist or not, not actually getting the thing done in the first place. The security guard can still shoot you, the vampire with Auspex still knows what you're going to do and can be in the right place at the right time, and so on.

> Defensive Driving
>
> Only usable by a minion with a vehicle.

> Minions without Celerity  get -1 intercept.

The problem with the whole "Minions with/without Celerity" thing is it's obviously more than a bit random. When it offers unblockability (as in the original suggestion), it's potentially a worthwhile deal - yes, it sometimes doesn't work, but when it does work it's really good. Here, I fear we're into the territory where it's a little too weak - you might include a couple if you're already playing vehicles, but will this incentivize many people to play a vehicle who weren't doing so already? Not so sure.

Also, in the "equipment/retainer that gives stealth" corner, you end up in the somewhat circular situation where if you don't have the stealth to get the equipment out in the first place, it's potentially a significant deck design and deck flow challenge. Say, you play in a group where Second Sight or weenie Auspex is fairly prevalent.

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> BenPeal wrote:
> Magic of the Smith for the vehicle itself or for a Pier 13 works pretty well.
>
Except that you're then probably playing Tremere and so get Thaumaturgy and Dominate, neither of which is terrible at delivery mechanisms - Seduction, Bonding, Mirror Walk, Sleeping Mind etc. Even Auspex can join in with Crocodile's Tongue which - at superior - is pretty solid. Even if playing weenie Thaumaturgy Cryptic Mission, you at least have access to Mirror Walk. I'd generally expect to see such decks playing those in preference to this, because it's just less hassle.

Here, I'd expect a card like this to be picked up more by clans/decks that lack a solid delivery mechanism, or whose delivery mechanism is quite awkward in some way e.g.

- annoying blood costs when you want to play weenies
- side effects like going to torpor from Day Op
- the delivery mechanism of your clan is mostly combat-oriented, and you'd prefer to avoid combat
- very, very limited for some reason

And for those sorts of situations, getting the equipment out onto one or more minions could be a pain in the ass, if your average tournament metagame includes things like Toreador 2nd Tradition, !Ven grinder, an Inbued deck, weenie Auspex, and a few well-timed DIs.
